s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging abdominal mass with intermittent high-grade fever and abdominal pain
salient_findings: Central abdominal lump
Intermittent high-grade fever
Dull, aching abdominal pain
Moderately tender mass in the umbilical region
Non-tender thickening of the right spermatic cord
Large, well-defined, unilocular cyst on abdominal ultrasonography
key_facts: 35-year-old man from rural north India
One-month history of progressively enlarging abdominal lump
Developed intermittent high-grade fever and abdominal pain three weeks after lump appeared
No significant past medical history
Moderately tender mass in the umbilical region on examination
Non-tender thickening of the right spermatic cord without scrotal or testicular abnormalities
Inguinal nodes were barely palpable
No lower-extremity edema
Complete blood counts and blood chemistry were within normal limits
Blood cultures were sterile
Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a large, well-defined, unilocular cyst
Contrast-enhanced CT scan confirmed ultrasonography findings
Surgical exploration revealed a large retroperitoneal cyst
Cyst was completely excised with a well-defined avascular plane

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Large, well-defined, unilocular cyst with dilated lymphatics near its upper pole

shortlist.label: Mesenteric cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst located behind the right colon and terminal ileum, consistent with mesenteric origin

shortlist.label: Cystic lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to retroperitoneal lymphangioma, with cystic and lymphatic components

shortlist.label: Enteric duplication cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst located near the terminal ileum, consistent with enteric duplication

shortlist.label: Mullerian duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst located in the retroperitoneum, consistent with Mullerian duct origin
